title: Readings on the companion and the witness geometry of a part

key_results.statement: For a part $A$ with companion $\bar A$: $(V_A)_{hh'}=\sum_k\Psi_{hk}\Psi_{h'k}^{*}$ is a finite sum over all joint places $k$ of $\bar A$, so $V_A$, and with it $X_V$, $\alpha$, $\sim$ and $\ell$, depends only on $|\Psi\rangle$ and the set $A$, not on how the companion is grouped or ordered.
Outcome probability of a reading on the companion: $p(r)=\sum_h\langle\psi_h|\Pi^{\bar A}_r|\psi_h\rangle=\sum_h\|\Pi^{\bar A}_r|\psi_h\rangle\|^2$, with $\sum_rp(r)=1$.
Post-reading state for an outcome with $p(r)>0$: $|\Psi_r\rangle=\Pi_r|\Psi\rangle/\sqrt{p(r)}=\sum_h|h\rangle\otimes\Pi^{\bar A}_r|\psi_h\rangle/\sqrt{p(r)}$.
Branch vectors of the post-reading state: $|\psi^{(r)}_h\rangle=\Pi^{\bar A}_r|\psi_h\rangle/\sqrt{p(r)}$.
View of the post-reading state: $(V_A(\Psi_r))_{hh'}=\langle\psi_{h'}|\Pi^{\bar A}_r|\psi_h\rangle/p(r)$, i.e. $V_A(\Psi_r)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\bar A}\big(\Pi_r|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|\big)/p(r)$.

For a label-free reading on the companion, $\Pi_r$ commutes with every swap iff (C): the class of $k$ does not depend on the places of the companion objects whose type occurs in $A$ (automatic when no type has objects on both sides of the cut); under (C) every $\Psi_r$ is admissible, and without (C) admissibility can fail (counterexample in Step 3e).
Outcome-averaged view: $\sum_rp(r)\,V_A(\Psi_r)=V_A(\Psi)$; neither label-freeness nor (C) is used.

For a local reading on $A$ with classes $S^A_s$: $\sum_rp(r)\,p(s\mid r)=\operatorname{Tr}\big(\Pi^A_sV_A(\Psi)\big)=p(s)$, so the outcome-averaged statistics of every local reading on $A$ do not depend on whether a distant reading on the companion was made, nor on which one was chosen.

For $h,h'\in H_V(\Psi_r)$: $W_r(h,h')=\frac{|\langle\psi_{h'}|\Pi^{\bar A}_r|\psi_h\rangle|^2}{\langle\psi_h|\Pi^{\bar A}_r|\psi_h\rangle\,\langle\psi_{h'}|\Pi^{\bar A}_r|\psi_{h'}\rangle}=|\langle e^{(r)}_{h'}|e^{(r)}_h\rangle|^2$ with $|e^{(r)}_h\rangle=\Pi^{\bar A}_r|\psi_h\rangle/\|\Pi^{\bar A}_r\psi_h\|$, and $\cos\alpha_r=\sqrt{W_r}$.

A reading on the companion never splits a point: if $h\approx h'$ in $\Psi$, then for every outcome both places are absent from $\Psi_r$ or both are present with $W_r(h,h')=1$; the map from the points of $X_V$ present in $\Psi_r$ to $X_V(\Psi_r)$ that sends $x$ to the point containing it is well defined and onto, so points can be removed or merged.

Example (two objects of different types; $A=\{1\}$ with places $\{0,1\}$, $\bar A=\{2\}$ with places $\{k_1,k_2,k_3\}$): for $|\Psi\rangle=\tfrac12\big(|0\rangle(|k_1\rangle+|k_2\rangle)+|1\rangle(|k_1\rangle+|k_3\rangle)\big)$ one has $(V_A)_{00}=(V_A)_{11}=\tfrac12$, $(V_A)_{01}=\tfrac14$, $W(0,1)=\tfrac14$ and $\alpha=\pi/3$, so the two points are distinct and $\ell\ge\pi/3$.

Same example, reading with classes $\{k_1\}$ and $\{k_2,k_3\}$, outcome 1: $p(1)=\tfrac12$, $|\Psi_1\rangle=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)\otimes|k_1\rangle$, $(V_A(\Psi_1))_{hh'}=\tfrac12$ for all $h,h'$, $W_1(0,1)=1$: the two points merge, $\alpha_1=0$ and $\ell_1=0$.

Same example, outcome 2: $p(2)=\tfrac12$, $|\Psi_2\rangle=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(|0\rangle|k_2\rangle+|1\rangle|k_3\rangle)$, $V_A(\Psi_2)=\tfrac12\mathbb 1$, $W_2(0,1)=0$: $\alpha_2=\pi/2$, the two points are no longer related and $\ell_2\ge\pi/2$.
Same example: $p(1)V_A(\Psi_1)+p(2)V_A(\Psi_2)=V_A(\Psi)$, so the outcome-averaged view is unchanged although $\alpha$ changes from $\pi/3$ to $0$ for outcome 1 and to $\pi/2$ for outcome 2.

If $\bar A=\bar A_1\cup\bar A_2$ and $|\Psi\rangle=|\Psi_{A\bar A_1}\rangle\otimes|\Omega_{\bar A_2}\rangle$, every reading on $\bar A_2$ alone has $p(r)=\langle\Omega|\Pi^{\bar A_2}_r|\Omega\rangle$ and $V_A(\Psi_r)=V_A(\Psi)$ for every outcome with $p(r)>0$, so $X_V$, $\alpha$, $\sim$ and $\ell$ are unchanged; label-freeness is not used.

open_issues: Discrepancy with the expected result of item 2: the lifted projector does not commute with every swap for every label-free reading on the companion; commutation, and with it admissibility, holds exactly under condition (C) of (9.7), in particular when no type has objects on both sides of the cut; the counterexample of Step 3e uses a cut that separates same-type instances, and whether such parts are legitimate is the open question of A7 and M6.

The exact values of ℓ in the two-point spaces of (9.13) and (9.15), either α or +∞, depend on the definition (4.3) of neighbours, which is quoted only as defined from α alone; the example uses only ℓ ≥ α and ℓ(x,x) = 0.
Notation: r labels outcomes and k labels the joint places of the companion; later packages that combine (2.1) with readings should keep this convention.

consistency_checks.check: Trivial reading: a single class gives p(1) = 1, Ψ₁ = Ψ and V_A(Ψ₁) = V_A(Ψ), and (9.11) reduces to (2.11).

Perfect record: if for each outcome at most one place has a nonzero projected branch vector, the branch vectors of different places are orthogonal, each post-reading state has a single present place (a single point), and the outcome average of the post-reading views equals V_A(Ψ), in agreement with (9.8).
Example average: (9.16), computed directly from the post-reading views (9.14) and (9.15), reproduces V_A(Ψ) of (9.13), as (9.8) requires.
